All timestamps on this page are UTC. + +To move around the timeline: + +- **Drag** to pan through time, or **scroll** to zoom in and out around the cursor +- Use the **zoom in** and **zoom out** buttons in the toolbar for fixed steps +- **Reset** returns to the default 7-day window and the default set of metrics +- **All off** clears the chart. **All on** turns on the CPU, memory, and summary metrics, but leaves per-device series off so the chart does not fill with one line per GPU + +Zooming in loads finer-grained data, down to per-second samples over short windows. + +## Detail tabs + +The bottom half of the page has three tabs, each showing detail for the time range currently in the chart. + +### Containers + +A timeline with one row per container that was on the machine during the window, so you can see the rental history at a glance: + +| Legend | What it shows | +| --- | --- | +| exists (stopped) | A thin gray line spanning the container's life. It existed on the machine but was not running | +| running | A solid blue bar over the periods the container was actually running | +| running (vm) | The same, in purple, for a container running as a VM | +| intermittent (zoom in) | A striped bar covering several runs and the gaps between them, too close together to draw separately at this zoom | + + + + + + +Hover a row for the container's status, last reported state, first and last seen times, how long it existed, and its run count and total running time. Click a run to zoom the chart to it and line the rental up with the GPU, memory, and network activity behind it. + + +A striped bar is a zoom artifact, not a problem. Zoom in to see the real pattern: restarts every few seconds are a crash loop, while a few runs spread over days is normal rental activity. + + +### Processes + +A table of the 50 heaviest processes in the window, ranked by accumulated CPU time: PID, command, CPU time, peak CPU percentage, peak resident memory, and first and last seen timestamps. Search and sorting work over those 50 rows, so narrow the time window to change which processes are in play. + +This includes processes running inside your clients' containers. + +### Logs + +The Vast daemon's log for that machine, with Info, Warning, Error, and Critical counts across the top. The counts cover the whole window; the lines below them are a capped sample of it. Click one or more severities to filter, or search to narrow by keyword. Repeated identical lines are grouped with a `×N` count rather than flooding the view. + + + + + + +Click a log line to pin a marker on the chart above and see what the machine was doing when the message was written. **Deselect All** clears the filters and any pinned markers. The refresh button re-runs the query for the current window; it does not move the window forward. + + +These are Vast daemon logs, not the logs from inside your clients' containers. Container output stays with the client's instance. + + +## Troubleshooting + +| Symptom | Where to look | +| --- | --- | +| A GPU running hot or throttling | Expand the GPU grid and compare Temperature, Power, and SM Clock per card. One card hotter and clocking lower than the rest points at cooling or seating rather than at the workload | +| Clients keep leaving the machine | Find the rental in the Containers tab and zoom into it. Short runs repeating back to back are a crash loop. Check the Logs tab around those times | +| Unexplained slowness | High CPU I/O Wait alongside disk utilization points at storage. High CPU Steal points at contention on the host | +| Bandwidth complaints | Chart Total RX and Total TX over the rental window, then expand the Network grid to check errors and drops on the interface | +| The machine looks idle | GPU utilization near zero through a rental usually means the client's workload is not using the GPUs | +| No data at all for a machine | It has most likely not reported yet. Check that it is online and running a current Vast daemon, and contact support if it stays empty | +| The chart stops short of right now | Expected. The page does not follow the clock. Reload it | + +## Limitations + +- **VM machines** report everything except GPU metrics for now. The page shows a notice when you are looking at one. +- **History starts when the machine first reported in its current recording format.** A recently set up machine has a shorter history than the default 7-day window, and a daemon update that changes the recording format restarts it. +- **There is no data deletion policy yet.** We will let hosts know if one is introduced.
